fr: Elle ne parle plus à sa sœur depuis leur dispute.
en: She no longer speaks to her sister since their argument.
ipa: /ɛl nə paʁl ply.z‿a sa sœʁ də.pɥi lœʁ dis.pyt/
notes: Liaison makes 'plus' sound like it ends in z before the vowel of 'à'; don't add an extra letter.

fr: Il n'a rien mangé depuis ce matin.
en: He hasn't eaten anything since this morning.
ipa: /il na ʁjɛ̃ mɑ̃.ʒe də.pɥi sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'ne' elides to n' before the vowel of 'a', a contraction easy to drop when writing fast.

fr: Nous n'avons aucune idée de l'heure qu'il est.
en: We have no idea what time it is.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃.z‿o.kyn i.de də lœʁ kil ɛ/
notes: 'aucune' takes the feminine e to agree with 'idée', a common agreement slip.

fr: Personne ne connaît la réponse à cette question.
en: Nobody knows the answer to this question.
ipa: /pɛʁ.sɔn nə kɔ.nɛ la ʁe.pɔ̃s a sɛt kɛs.tjɔ̃/
notes: 'Personne' as subject still requires 'ne' before the verb, unlike in casual spoken French.

fr: Je ne mange que des légumes le soir.
en: I only eat vegetables in the evening.
ipa: /ʒə nə mɑ̃ʒ kə de le.ɡym lə swaʁ/
notes: 'ne...que' expresses a restriction, so don't write it as a full negation like 'ne...pas'.

fr: Ces enfants ne jouent jamais dans le jardin.
en: These children never play in the garden.
ipa: /se.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ nə ʒu ʒa.mɛ dɑ̃ lə ʒaʁ.dɛ̃/
notes: 'Ces' sounds exactly like 'ses' and 'c'est'; only context decides which spelling to use.

fr: Il ne sait pas quelle heure il est.
en: He doesn't know what time it is.
ipa: /il nə sɛ pa kɛl œʁ il ɛ/
notes: 'quelle' is pronounced like 'quel', 'qu'elle', and 'quels'; the ending only shows in writing.

fr: Nous ne sortons plus le week-end.
en: We no longer go out on weekends.
ipa: /nu nə sɔʁ.tɔ̃ ply lə wik.ɛnd/
notes: Before a consonant, the final 's' of 'plus' stays silent in this negative sense.

fr: Elle n'a aucun ami dans cette ville.
en: She has no friends in this town.
ipa: /ɛl na o.kœ̃.n‿a.mi dɑ̃ sɛt vil/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'aucun' must keep its 'un' spelling even though it isn't a full consonant sound.

fr: Ils n'ont ni argent ni temps pour voyager.
en: They have neither money nor time to travel.
ipa: /il nɔ̃ ni aʁ.ʒɑ̃ ni tɑ̃ puʁ vwa.ja.ʒe/
notes: 'ni...ni' replaces both 'et' and the usual 'pas'; don't add 'pas' as well.

fr: Je n'ai plus confiance en cet homme.
en: I no longer trust that man.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ ply kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s ɑ̃ sɛ.t‿ɔm/
notes: 'cet' is used before a vowel sound, while sounding just like 'cette'.

fr: On ne voit personne à cette heure de la nuit.
en: You don't see anyone at this hour of the night.
ipa: /ɔ̃ nə vwa pɛʁ.sɔn a sɛt œʁ də la nɥi/
notes: 'On' and 'ont' sound identical; here 'on' is the subject pronoun, not the verb 'avoir'.

fr: Elle n'a pas encore fini ses devoirs.
en: She hasn't finished her homework yet.
ipa: /ɛl na pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ fi.ni se də.vwaʁ/
notes: Liaison joins 'pas' and 'encore' with a z sound not written as a separate letter.

fr: Nous n'avons rien contre cette décision.
en: We have nothing against this decision.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ kɔ̃tʁ sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃/
notes: The nasal 'ien' in 'rien' is one glide-vowel sound, not two separate vowels.

fr: Il ne reste que deux places pour le concert.
en: There are only two seats left for the concert.
ipa: /il nə ʁɛst kə dø plas puʁ lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ/
notes: 'que' here marks restriction, so the final 't' of 'concert' still stays silent as usual.

fr: Ma tante ne conduit plus depuis son accident.
en: My aunt no longer drives since her accident.
ipa: /ma tɑ̃t nə kɔ̃.dɥi ply də.pɥi sɔ.n‿ak.si.dɑ̃/
notes: Liaison links 'son' and 'accident' with a hidden n sound.

fr: Je ne pense pas qu'il vienne à la réunion.
en: I don't think he'll come to the meeting.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kil vjɛn a la ʁe.y.njɔ̃/
notes: After 'ne pas penser que', the verb switches to the subjunctive 'vienne', not 'vient'.

fr: Elle ne se souvient d'aucun détail de la soirée.
en: She doesn't remember any detail from the evening.
ipa: /ɛl nə sə su.vjɛ̃ do.kœ̃ de.taj də la swa.ʁe/
notes: 'd'aucun' contracts 'de' before the vowel of 'aucun'.

fr: Nous n'avons vu personne dans le couloir.
en: We didn't see anyone in the hallway.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ vy pɛʁ.sɔn dɑ̃ lə ku.lwaʁ/
notes: 'personne' as object needs no extra negative word; 'ne...personne' alone is complete.

fr: Il n'a jamais menti à ses parents.
en: He has never lied to his parents.
ipa: /il na ʒa.mɛ mɑ̃.ti a se pa.ʁɑ̃/
notes: 'ses' sounds like 'ces' and 'c'est'; only the meaning tells them apart.

fr: Je ne mangerai plus jamais dans ce restaurant.
en: I will never eat at this restaurant again.
ipa: /ʒə nə mɑ̃ʒ.ʁɛ ply ʒa.mɛ dɑ̃ sə ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃/
notes: The future ending '-erai' keeps a mute e before the r that changes the sound of the verb stem.

fr: Elle n'aime pas qu'on lui pose trop de questions.
en: She doesn't like people asking her too many questions.
ipa: /ɛl nɛm pa kɔ̃ lɥi poz tʁo də kɛs.tjɔ̃/
notes: 'qu'on' elides 'que' before the vowel of 'on'.

fr: Nous ne ferons rien sans son accord.
en: We won't do anything without her approval.
ipa: /nu nə fə.ʁɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ sɑ̃ sɔ.n‿a.kɔʁ/
notes: Liaison joins 'son' and 'accord' with a linking n.

fr: Il ne reconnaît aucune de ces photos.
en: He doesn't recognize any of these photos.
ipa: /il nə ʁə.kɔ.nɛ o.kyn də se fo.to/
notes: 'aucune' must agree with the feminine 'photo' even though it stands for a plural group.

fr: Elle ne travaille que le matin cette semaine.
en: She only works in the mornings this week.
ipa: /ɛl nə tʁa.vaj kə lə ma.tɛ̃ sɛt sə.mɛn/
notes: 'cette' before a consonant is the standard feminine spelling of 'ce'.

fr: Je n'ai vu ni le chat ni le chien aujourd'hui.
en: I saw neither the cat nor the dog today.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ vy ni lə ʃa ni lə ʃjɛ̃ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: Since 'le chat' and 'le chien' are definite, the article stays after each 'ni'.

fr: Ils n'habitent plus dans cet immeuble.
en: They no longer live in this building.
ipa: /il na.bit ply dɑ̃ sɛ.t‿i.mœbl/
notes: 'cet' is used before a vowel sound, here 'immeuble', instead of 'ce'.

fr: Je ne crois pas que ce soit une bonne idée.
en: I don't think that's a good idea.
ipa: /ʒə nə kʁwa pa kə sə swa yn bɔn i.de/
notes: After 'ne pas croire que', 'être' switches to the subjunctive form 'soit'.

fr: Nous n'avons pas encore reçu de réponse.
en: We haven't received a reply yet.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ ʁə.sy də ʁe.pɔ̃s/
notes: The past participle 'reçu' keeps its cedilla so the c stays soft before u.

fr: Elle ne veut voir personne ce soir.
en: She doesn't want to see anyone tonight.
ipa: /ɛl nə vø vwaʁ pɛʁ.sɔn sə swaʁ/
notes: 'ce soir' uses the demonstrative 'ce', not the reflexive 'se', even though they sound alike.

fr: Il n'a plus aucune raison de s'inquiéter.
en: He no longer has any reason to worry.
ipa: /il na ply.z‿o.kyn ʁɛ.zɔ̃ də sɛ̃.kje.te/
notes: 'plus' and 'aucune' combine for emphasis; liaison links them with a z sound.

fr: Je ne comprends rien à cet exercice.
en: I don't understand anything about this exercise.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ ʁjɛ̃ a sɛ.t‿ɛg.zɛʁ.sis/
notes: The ending '-ends' of 'comprends' is silent; only the nasal vowel before it is heard.

fr: Nous ne partirons que demain matin.
en: We won't leave until tomorrow morning.
ipa: /nu nə paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ kə də.mɛ̃ ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'ne...que' here means 'not until', a restrictive sense easy to confuse with plain negation.

fr: Elle ne sort avec aucun de ses collègues.
en: She doesn't go out with any of her colleagues.
ipa: /ɛl nə sɔʁ a.vɛk o.kœ̃ də se kɔ.lɛg/
notes: 'aucun' stays masculine here because it refers to 'collègue' used generically.

fr: Il n'y a plus rien dans le frigo.
en: There's nothing left in the fridge.
ipa: /il ni.a ply ʁjɛ̃ dɑ̃ lə fʁi.go/
notes: 'n'y a' contracts 'ne' before the pronoun 'y', itself placed before 'a'.

fr: Je ne connais aucun restaurant ouvert ce lundi.
en: I don't know of any restaurant open this Monday.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ o.kœ̃ ʁɛs.to.ʁɑ̃ u.vɛʁ sə lœ̃.di/
notes: The nasal vowel of 'aucun' and of 'lundi' are the same sound, both spelled with 'un'.

fr: Elle ne veut plus jamais revivre cette expérience.
en: She never wants to relive that experience again.
ipa: /ɛl nə vø ply ʒa.mɛ ʁə.vivʁ sɛ.t‿ɛks.pe.ʁjɑ̃s/
notes: 'cette' before a vowel sound still keeps its double t, unlike 'cet'.

fr: Nous n'avons aucun doute sur sa sincérité.
en: We have no doubt about her sincerity.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃.z‿o.kœ̃ dut syʁ sa sɛ̃.se.ʁi.te/
notes: Liaison links 'avons' and 'aucun' with a z sound not shown by a separate letter.

fr: Il ne mange jamais de viande le vendredi.
en: He never eats meat on Fridays.
ipa: /il nə mɑ̃ʒ ʒa.mɛ də vjɑ̃d lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
notes: After 'jamais', the partitive article drops to simply 'de', not 'de la' or 'du'.

fr: Je n'ose pas lui dire la vérité.
en: I don't dare tell him the truth.
ipa: /ʒə noz pa lɥi diʁ la ve.ʁi.te/
notes: 'ne' elides to n' before the vowel-initial verb 'ose'.

fr: Elle ne reconnaît plus personne dans sa famille.
en: She no longer recognizes anyone in her family.
ipa: /ɛl nə ʁə.kɔ.nɛ ply pɛʁ.sɔn dɑ̃ sa fa.mij/
notes: Two negative words, 'plus' and 'personne', combine without adding 'pas'.

fr: Nous ne savons pas ce qu'il pense vraiment.
en: We don't know what he really thinks.
ipa: /nu nə sa.vɔ̃ pa sə kil pɑ̃s vʁɛ.mɑ̃/
notes: 'ce qu'il' uses the demonstrative 'ce', not the homophone reflexive 'se'.

fr: Il n'a aucun problème avec ses collègues.
en: He has no problem with his colleagues.
ipa: /il na o.kœ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm a.vɛk se kɔ.lɛg/
notes: 'ses' is the plural possessive, pronounced exactly like 'ces' and 'c'est'.

fr: Elle ne boit plus de café le soir.
en: She no longer drinks coffee in the evening.
ipa: /ɛl nə bwa ply də ka.fe lə swaʁ/
notes: After a negation, the article becomes simply 'de', replacing 'du'.

fr: Je ne sors avec personne en ce moment.
en: I'm not dating anyone right now.
ipa: /ʒə nə sɔʁ a.vɛk pɛʁ.sɔn ɑ̃ sə mo.mɑ̃/
notes: 'ce moment' uses the demonstrative 'ce', spelled differently from the reflexive 'se'.

fr: Nous n'avons plus aucun contact avec eux.
en: We no longer have any contact with them.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ply.z‿o.kœ̃ kɔ̃.takt a.vɛk ø/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' and 'aucun' before the nasal vowel.

fr: Il ne reste plus que quelques minutes avant le départ.
en: There are only a few minutes left before departure.
ipa: /il nə ʁɛst ply kə kɛl.kə mi.nyt a.vɑ̃ lə de.paʁ/
notes: 'plus que' combines 'no longer' and 'only'; both negative words stay before the complement.

fr: Elle n'a jamais aimé les épinards.
en: She has never liked spinach.
ipa: /ɛl na ʒa.mɛ ɛ.me le.z‿e.pi.naʁ/
notes: Liaison links the plural article 'les' to the vowel of 'épinards'.

fr: Je ne veux rien savoir de cette histoire.
en: I don't want to know anything about this story.
ipa: /ʒə nə vø ʁjɛ̃ sa.vwaʁ də sɛt is.twaʁ/
notes: 'cette' keeps its silent final e before the consonant sound of 'histoire'.

fr: Nous ne recevons aucune aide de la mairie.
en: We don't receive any help from the town hall.
ipa: /nu nə ʁə.sə.vɔ̃.z‿o.kyn ɛd də la mɛ.ʁi/
notes: 'aucune' takes the feminine ending to agree with 'aide'.

fr: Il ne se rappelle plus du tout de ce film.
en: He doesn't remember that film at all.
ipa: /il nə sə ʁa.pɛl ply dy tu də sə film/
notes: 'ne...plus du tout' intensifies the negation; don't drop the 'ne' when writing.

fr: Elle ne fait confiance qu'à sa meilleure amie.
en: She only trusts her best friend.
ipa: /ɛl nə fɛ kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s ka sa mɛ.jœʁ a.mi/
notes: 'qu'à' contracts 'que' before the preposition 'à', both pronounced together.

fr: Je n'ai aucune envie de sortir aujourd'hui.
en: I have no desire to go out today.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ o.kyn ɑ̃.vi də sɔʁ.tiʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: The nasal 'en' of 'envie' should not be spelled 'an', though the two sound identical.

fr: Nous ne dormons jamais avant minuit.
en: We never sleep before midnight.
ipa: /nu nə dɔʁ.mɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ a.vɑ̃ mi.nɥi/
notes: The final 's' of both 'dormons' and 'jamais' is silent and easy to forget in dictation.

fr: Il ne veut plus jamais revoir son ex-femme.
en: He never wants to see his ex-wife again.
ipa: /il nə vø ply ʒa.mɛ ʁə.vwaʁ sɔ.n‿ɛks.fam/
notes: Liaison links the possessive 'son' to the vowel-initial 'ex-femme'.

fr: Elle ne mange que du poisson le vendredi.
en: She only eats fish on Fridays.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ʒ kə dy pwa.sɔ̃ lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di/
notes: 'que' here restricts the meaning to 'only', unlike the relative pronoun 'que'.

fr: Je ne vois aucun inconvénient à ce projet.
en: I see no problem with this project.
ipa: /ʒə nə vwa o.kœ̃.n‿ɛ̃.kɔ̃.ve.njɑ̃ a sə pʁɔ.ʒɛ/
notes: Liaison joins 'aucun' and 'inconvénient' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Nous n'avons ni le temps ni l'envie de discuter.
en: We have neither the time nor the desire to discuss it.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ni lə tɑ̃ ni lɑ̃.vi də dis.ky.te/
notes: The second 'ni' elides its following article, 'l'envie', before a vowel.

fr: Elle n'ira jamais dans ce quartier seule.
en: She will never go into that neighborhood alone.
ipa: /ɛl ni.ʁa ʒa.mɛ dɑ̃ sə kaʁ.tje sœl/
notes: 'n'ira' elides 'ne' before the future form of 'aller', which starts with a vowel.

fr: Il ne reconnaît aucun mérite à ses collègues.
en: He gives his colleagues no credit at all.
ipa: /il nə ʁə.kɔ.nɛ o.kœ̃ me.ʁit a se kɔ.lɛg/
notes: 'ses' possessive plural is a classic homophone trap with 'ces' and 'c'est'.

fr: Nous ne changerons rien à nos habitudes.
en: We won't change anything about our habits.
ipa: /nu nə ʃɑ̃ʒ.ʁɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ a no.z‿a.bi.tyd/
notes: Liaison links the plural 'nos' to the vowel of 'habitudes'.

fr: Je ne pense pas que ce soit nécessaire.
en: I don't think that's necessary.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə swa ne.se.sɛʁ/
notes: The subjunctive 'soit' follows negated opinion verbs like 'penser'.

fr: Elle n'a plus aucune patience avec ses élèves.
en: She has no more patience with her students.
ipa: /ɛl na ply.z‿o.kyn pa.sjɑ̃s a.vɛk se.z‿e.lɛv/
notes: Two liaisons appear here: 'plus aucune' and 'ses élèves'.

fr: Il ne se souvient de rien après l'accident.
en: He remembers nothing after the accident.
ipa: /il nə sə su.vjɛ̃ də ʁjɛ̃ a.pʁɛ lak.si.dɑ̃/
notes: 'l'accident' elides the article 'le' before the vowel.

fr: Nous ne mangeons jamais de viande rouge.
en: We never eat red meat.
ipa: /nu nə mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ də vjɑ̃d ʁuʒ/
notes: The extra 'e' in 'mangeons' keeps the g soft before o; it isn't a mistake.

fr: Je n'ai vu personne au marché ce matin.
en: I didn't see anyone at the market this morning.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ vy pɛʁ.sɔn o maʁ.ʃe sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'au' contracts 'à' and 'le'; there's no separate written word for 'the' here.

fr: Elle ne conduit que le week-end maintenant.
en: She only drives on weekends now.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɔ̃.dɥi kə lə wik.ɛnd mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃/
notes: 'que' restricts to 'only'; keep the full 'ne...que' pair when writing.

fr: Il n'a aucune idée de ce qui s'est passé.
en: He has no idea what happened.
ipa: /il na o.kyn i.de də sə ki sɛ pa.se/
notes: 's'est' sounds like 'c'est'; only context distinguishes the reflexive from the pronoun.

fr: Nous ne voulons plus entendre parler de lui.
en: We no longer want to hear about him.
ipa: /nu nə vu.lɔ̃ ply.z‿ɑ̃.tɑ̃dʁ paʁ.le də lɥi/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' to 'entendre' with a z sound.

fr: Je ne trouve nulle part mes clés ce matin.
en: I can't find my keys anywhere this morning.
ipa: /ʒə nə tʁuv nyl paʁ me kle sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'nulle part' is a fixed negative expression meaning 'nowhere'; 'nulle' keeps its double l.

fr: Elle ne pardonnera jamais cette trahison.
en: She will never forgive that betrayal.
ipa: /ɛl nə paʁ.dɔ.nə.ʁa ʒa.mɛ sɛt tʁa.i.zɔ̃/
notes: The future ending '-era' keeps a mute e that softens the pronunciation of the stem.

fr: Nous n'avons trouvé aucun signe de vie.
en: We found no sign of life.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ tʁu.ve o.kœ̃ siɲ də vi/
notes: 'aucun' agrees with the masculine 'signe', not with the feminine 'vie'.

fr: Il ne veut jamais admettre ses erreurs.
en: He never wants to admit his mistakes.
ipa: /il nə vø ʒa.mɛ ad.mɛtʁ se.z‿e.ʁœʁ/
notes: Liaison links 'ses' to the vowel of 'erreurs' with a z sound.

fr: Je ne bois plus jamais d'alcool le soir.
en: I never drink alcohol in the evening anymore.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa ply ʒa.mɛ dal.kɔl lə swaʁ/
notes: 'd'alcool' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Elle ne connaît personne dans cette entreprise.
en: She doesn't know anyone at this company.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɔ.nɛ pɛʁ.sɔn dɑ̃ sɛ.t‿ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz/
notes: 'cette' before the vowel of 'entreprise' still uses its double-t spelling.

fr: Nous ne ferons aucun commentaire pour l'instant.
en: We won't make any comment for now.
ipa: /nu nə fə.ʁɔ̃ o.kœ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.tɛʁ puʁ lɛ̃s.tɑ̃/
notes: 'l'instant' elides 'le' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Il n'écoute jamais les conseils de ses amis.
en: He never listens to his friends' advice.
ipa: /il ne.kut ʒa.mɛ le kɔ̃.sɛj də se.z‿a.mi/
notes: 'n'écoute' elides 'ne' before the vowel-initial verb.

fr: Je ne regrette rien de ce que j'ai fait.
en: I regret nothing that I did.
ipa: /ʒə nə ʁə.gʁɛt ʁjɛ̃ də sə kə ʒe fɛ/
notes: 'ce que' is often mixed up with 'ceux que' in fast dictation, though the two sound different.

fr: Elle n'a aucun regret depuis son départ.
en: She has no regrets since her departure.
ipa: /ɛl na o.kœ̃ ʁə.gʁɛ də.pɥi sɔ̃ de.paʁ/
notes: The nasal vowel of 'aucun' must be spelled with 'un', not 'in' or 'en'.

fr: Nous ne sommes plus amis depuis cette dispute.
en: We are no longer friends since that argument.
ipa: /nu sɔm ply.z‿a.mi də.pɥi sɛt dis.pyt/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' and 'amis' with a z sound in this negation.

fr: Il ne fait jamais ses devoirs à temps.
en: He never does his homework on time.
ipa: /il nə fɛ ʒa.mɛ se də.vwaʁ a tɑ̃/
notes: 'ses' possessive is identical in sound to 'ces' and 'c'est'.

fr: Je ne mangerais jamais ce genre de plat.
en: I would never eat that kind of dish.
ipa: /ʒə nə mɑ̃ʒ.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ sə ʒɑ̃ʁ də pla/
notes: The conditional ending '-rais' sounds like the imperfect '-rais' too; only context tells them apart.

fr: Elle ne trouve aucun intérêt à ce sujet.
en: She finds no interest in this topic.
ipa: /ɛl nə tʁuv o.kœ̃.n‿ɛ̃.te.ʁɛ a sə sy.ʒɛ/
notes: Liaison links 'aucun' and 'intérêt' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Nous n'osons plus lui poser de questions.
en: We no longer dare ask him questions.
ipa: /nu no.zɔ̃ ply lɥi po.ze də kɛs.tjɔ̃/
notes: 'n'osons' elides 'ne' before the vowel-initial verb 'osons'.

fr: Il ne reste aucune trace de cet incident.
en: There is no trace left of that incident.
ipa: /il nə ʁɛst o.kyn tʁas də sɛ.t‿ɛ̃.si.dɑ̃/
notes: 'aucune' agrees with the feminine 'trace', while 'cet' agrees with the masculine 'incident'.

fr: Je ne dis jamais de mal de mes collègues.
en: I never speak badly of my colleagues.
ipa: /ʒə nə di ʒa.mɛ də mal də me kɔ.lɛg/
notes: 'mes' sounds like 'mais'; only spelling separates the possessive from the conjunction.

fr: Elle n'a plus rien à perdre maintenant.
en: She has nothing more to lose now.
ipa: /ɛl na ply ʁjɛ̃ a pɛʁdʁ mɛ̃.tə.nɑ̃/
notes: 'plus rien' stacks two negative words without adding 'pas'.

fr: Nous ne savons pas encore où aller.
en: We don't know yet where to go.
ipa: /nu nə sa.vɔ̃ pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ u a.le/
notes: Liaison links 'pas' and 'encore' with a z sound.

fr: Il n'accepte jamais les critiques de son patron.
en: He never accepts criticism from his boss.
ipa: /il nak.sɛpt ʒa.mɛ le kʁi.tik də sɔ̃ pa.tʁɔ̃/
notes: 'n'accepte' elides 'ne' before the vowel-initial verb.

fr: Je ne connais aucune solution à ce problème.
en: I know no solution to this problem.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ o.kyn sɔ.ly.sjɔ̃ a sə pʁɔ.blɛm/
notes: 'aucune' agrees with the feminine 'solution'.

fr: Elle ne parle à personne de ses soucis.
en: She doesn't talk to anyone about her worries.
ipa: /ɛl nə paʁl a pɛʁ.sɔn də se su.si/
notes: 'ses' versus 'ces' is a classic dictée homophone trap for possessive and demonstrative.

fr: Nous n'avons plus le temps de discuter.
en: We no longer have time to discuss it.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ply lə tɑ̃ də dis.ky.te/
notes: The word 'temps' ends in a silent 'ps' that is easy to forget when writing.

fr: Il ne se plaint jamais de rien.
en: He never complains about anything.
ipa: /il nə sə plɛ̃ ʒa.mɛ də ʁjɛ̃/
notes: 'se plaint' uses the reflexive 'se', not the demonstrative 'ce'.

fr: Je n'ai aucun doute sur ses intentions.
en: I have no doubt about his intentions.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ o.kœ̃ dut syʁ se.z‿ɛ̃.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃/
notes: Liaison links 'ses' and 'intentions' with a z sound.

fr: Elle ne prend jamais de dessert après le dîner.
en: She never has dessert after dinner.
ipa: /ɛl nə pʁɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ də de.sɛʁ a.pʁɛ lə di.ne/
notes: After a negation, 'du dessert' becomes simply 'de dessert'.

fr: Nous ne comprenons rien à ces instructions.
en: We understand nothing about these instructions.
ipa: /nu nə kɔ̃.pʁə.nɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ a se.z‿ɛ̃s.tʁyk.sjɔ̃/
notes: 'ces' is a homophone of 'ses' and 'c'est'.

fr: Il n'a pas encore choisi son sujet de thèse.
en: He hasn't chosen his thesis topic yet.
ipa: /il na pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ ʃwa.zi sɔ̃ sy.ʒɛ də tɛz/
notes: Liaison connects 'pas' and 'encore' with a z sound.

fr: Je ne veux plus jamais entendre parler de ça.
en: I never want to hear about that again.
ipa: /ʒə nə vø ply ʒa.mɛ ɑ̃.tɑ̃dʁ paʁ.le də sa/
notes: 'ça' is spelled with a cedilla to keep the soft s sound before 'a'.

fr: Elle n'a confiance en aucun de ses voisins.
en: She trusts none of her neighbors.
ipa: /ɛl na kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s ɑ̃ o.kœ̃ də se vwa.zɛ̃/
notes: 'aucun' stays masculine to match the generic noun 'voisin'.

fr: Le comité ne peut rien décider sans l'accord du directeur.
en: The committee cannot decide anything without the director's approval.
ipa: /lə kɔ.mi.te nə pø ʁjɛ̃ de.si.de sɑ̃ la.kɔʁ dy di.ʁɛk.tœʁ/
notes: 'l'accord' elides the article 'le' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Il ne mange plus de sucre depuis un an.
en: He hasn't eaten sugar for a year.
ipa: /il nə mɑ̃ʒ ply də sykʁ də.pɥi œ̃.n‿ɑ̃/
notes: Liaison links 'un' and 'an' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Je ne connais aucun de ses amis d'enfance.
en: I don't know any of her childhood friends.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ o.kœ̃ də se.z‿a.mi dɑ̃.fɑ̃s/
notes: 'd'enfance' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Elle ne cuisine jamais sans huile d'olive.
en: She never cooks without olive oil.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɥi.zin ʒa.mɛ sɑ̃.z‿ɥil dɔ.liv/
notes: Liaison links 'sans' and 'huile' with a z sound, since the h of 'huile' is mute.

fr: Nous n'avons aucun regret d'être partis.
en: We have no regret about having left.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ o.kœ̃ ʁə.gʁɛ dɛtʁ paʁ.ti/
notes: 'd'être' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial infinitive.

fr: Il ne parle jamais de son travail à la maison.
en: He never talks about his work at home.
ipa: /il nə paʁl ʒa.mɛ də sɔ̃ tʁa.vaj a la mɛ.zɔ̃/
notes: The nasal 'on' in 'son' must not be confused with the verb form 'sont'.

fr: Je ne bois que de l'eau pendant les repas.
en: I only drink water during meals.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa kə də lo pɑ̃.dɑ̃ le ʁə.pa/
notes: 'de l'eau' elides the article 'la' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Elle n'a jamais quitté sa ville natale.
en: She has never left her hometown.
ipa: /ɛl na ʒa.mɛ ki.te sa vil na.tal/
notes: 'quitté' keeps its accented é even after the negative particle 'jamais'.

fr: Nous ne recevons plus aucune lettre de lui.
en: We no longer receive any letter from him.
ipa: /nu nə ʁə.sə.vɔ̃ ply.z‿o.kyn lɛtʁ də lɥi/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' and 'aucune' before the vowel.

fr: Il ne sait jamais quoi répondre.
en: He never knows what to answer.
ipa: /il nə sɛ ʒa.mɛ kwa ʁe.pɔ̃dʁ/
notes: 'sait' and 'ses' sound similar but are never interchangeable in writing.

fr: Je ne trouve aucune excuse à son retard.
en: I find no excuse for his lateness.
ipa: /ʒə nə tʁuv o.kyn ɛks.kyz a sɔ̃ ʁə.taʁ/
notes: 'aucune' agrees with the feminine 'excuse'.

fr: Elle ne travaille jamais le dimanche.
en: She never works on Sundays.
ipa: /ɛl nə tʁa.vaj ʒa.mɛ lə di.mɑ̃ʃ/
notes: The nasal 'an' in 'dimanche' is spelled 'an', unlike the similar-sounding 'en'.

fr: Nous ne voyons plus personne depuis le confinement.
en: We haven't seen anyone since the lockdown.
ipa: /nu nə vwa.jɔ̃ ply pɛʁ.sɔn də.pɥi lə kɔ̃.fin.mɑ̃/
notes: 'plus personne' combines two negative words without adding 'pas'.

fr: Il n'accorde aucune importance à l'argent.
en: He attaches no importance to money.
ipa: /il na.kɔʁd o.kyn ɛ̃.pɔʁ.tɑ̃s a laʁ.ʒɑ̃/
notes: 'l'argent' elides the article 'le' before the vowel.

fr: Je ne bois jamais d'alcool avant de conduire.
en: I never drink alcohol before driving.
ipa: /ʒə nə bwa ʒa.mɛ dal.kɔl a.vɑ̃ də kɔ̃.dɥiʁ/
notes: 'd'alcool' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Elle ne veut épouser personne pour l'instant.
en: She doesn't want to marry anyone for now.
ipa: /ɛl nə vø e.pu.ze pɛʁ.sɔn puʁ lɛ̃s.tɑ̃/
notes: 'l'instant' elides 'le' before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Nous n'avons aucune preuve contre lui.
en: We have no proof against him.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ o.kyn pʁœv kɔ̃tʁ lɥi/
notes: 'aucune' agrees with the feminine 'preuve'.

fr: Il ne se souvient jamais de mon anniversaire.
en: He never remembers my birthday.
ipa: /il nə sə su.vjɛ̃ ʒa.mɛ də mɔ.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ/
notes: Liaison links 'mon' and 'anniversaire' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Je ne veux rien entendre de plus.
en: I don't want to hear anything more.
ipa: /ʒə nə vø ʁjɛ̃.n‿ɑ̃.tɑ̃dʁ də plys/
notes: Liaison links 'rien' to 'entendre' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Elle ne connaît aucun de ses voisins actuels.
en: She doesn't know any of her current neighbors.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɔ.nɛ o.kœ̃ də se vwa.zɛ̃ ak.tɥɛl/
notes: 'ses' possessive plural mirrors the sound of 'ces' and 'c'est'.

fr: Nous ne partons jamais sans nos passeports.
en: We never leave without our passports.
ipa: /nu nə paʁ.tɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ sɑ̃ no pas.pɔʁ/
notes: The final 's' of 'passeports' stays silent in standard pronunciation.

fr: Il n'a plus aucune envie de discuter.
en: He has no more desire to talk.
ipa: /il na ply.z‿o.kyn ɑ̃.vi də dis.ky.te/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' and 'aucune' with a z sound before the nasal vowel.

fr: Je ne mange rien après huit heures du soir.
en: I eat nothing after eight in the evening.
ipa: /ʒə nə mɑ̃ʒ ʁjɛ̃ a.pʁɛ ɥi.t‿œʁ dy swaʁ/
notes: Liaison links 'huit' and 'heures' even though 'huit' normally ends in a silent t.

fr: Elle n'accepte aucune excuse de sa part.
en: She accepts no excuse from him or her.
ipa: /ɛl nak.sɛpt o.kyn ɛks.kyz də sa paʁ/
notes: 'n'accepte' elides 'ne' before the vowel-initial verb.

fr: Nous ne dépensons jamais plus que nécessaire.
en: We never spend more than necessary.
ipa: /nu nə de.pɑ̃.sɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ plys kə ne.se.sɛʁ/
notes: Here 'plus' keeps its final s sound because it means 'more', not the negative 'no longer'.

fr: Il ne fait confiance à personne d'autre.
en: He trusts no one else.
ipa: /il nə fɛ kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s a pɛʁ.sɔn dotʁ/
notes: 'd'autre' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial adjective.

fr: Je n'ai aucune envie de retourner là-bas.
en: I have no desire to go back there.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ o.kyn ɑ̃.vi də ʁə.tuʁ.ne la.ba/
notes: 'là-bas' uses a grave accent on 'là' to distinguish it from the article 'la'.

fr: Elle ne pardonne jamais un mensonge.
en: She never forgives a lie.
ipa: /ɛl nə paʁ.dɔn ʒa.mɛ œ̃ mɑ̃.sɔ̃ʒ/
notes: 'mensonge' has two nasal vowels, 'en' then 'on'; both must be spelled correctly.

fr: Nous ne savons rien de son passé.
en: We know nothing about his past.
ipa: /nu nə sa.vɔ̃ ʁjɛ̃ də sɔ̃ pa.se/
notes: 'son' must not be confused with the plural verb form 'sont'.

fr: Il n'a plus aucun ami depuis son déménagement.
en: He has no more friends since he moved.
ipa: /il na ply.z‿o.kœ̃.n‿a.mi də.pɥi sɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒə.mɑ̃/
notes: Two liaisons chain together here, 'plus aucun' and 'aucun ami'.

fr: Je ne trouve nulle trace de mon passeport.
en: I can't find any trace of my passport.
ipa: /ʒə nə tʁuv nyl tʁas də mɔ̃ pas.pɔʁ/
notes: 'nulle' agrees in the feminine with 'trace', keeping its double l.

fr: Elle ne ment jamais à ses amis proches.
en: She never lies to her close friends.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ a se.z‿a.mi pʁɔʃ/
notes: Liaison links 'ses' and 'amis' with a z sound.

fr: Nous n'avons plus rien à nous dire.
en: We have nothing left to say to each other.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ ply ʁjɛ̃ a nu diʁ/
notes: 'plus rien' stacks two negatives before the infinitive.

fr: Il ne comprend jamais mes explications.
en: He never understands my explanations.
ipa: /il nə kɔ̃.pʁɑ̃ ʒa.mɛ me.z‿ɛks.pli.ka.sjɔ̃/
notes: Liaison links 'mes' to 'explications' with a z sound.

fr: Je ne veux aucun cadeau pour mon anniversaire.
en: I don't want any present for my birthday.
ipa: /ʒə nə vø o.kœ̃ ka.do puʁ mɔ.n‿a.ni.vɛʁ.sɛʁ/
notes: Liaison links 'mon' and 'anniversaire' with a nasal n sound.

fr: Elle n'a aucun scrupule à mentir.
en: She has no qualms about lying.
ipa: /ɛl na o.kœ̃ skʁy.pyl a mɑ̃.tiʁ/
notes: 'scrupule' keeps its silent final e, pronounced without adding an extra syllable.

fr: Nous ne voulons plus jamais revivre cette période.
en: We never want to relive that period again.
ipa: /nu nə vu.lɔ̃ ply ʒa.mɛ ʁə.vivʁ sɛt pe.ʁjɔd/
notes: 'cette' keeps its double t before the consonant of 'période'.

fr: Il ne se fie qu'à son instinct.
en: He only trusts his instinct.
ipa: /il nə sə fi ka sɔ.n‿ɛ̃s.tɛ̃kt/
notes: 'qu'à' contracts 'que' before the preposition 'à'.

fr: Je n'ai jamais eu aucun problème avec elle.
en: I have never had any problem with her.
ipa: /ʒə nɛ ʒa.mɛ.z‿y o.kœ̃ pʁɔ.blɛm a.vɛk ɛl/
notes: Liaison links 'jamais' and 'eu' with a z sound.

fr: Elle ne raconte jamais rien de personnel.
en: She never tells anything personal.
ipa: /ɛl nə ʁa.kɔ̃t ʒa.mɛ ʁjɛ̃ də pɛʁ.sɔ.nɛl/
notes: 'personnel' doubles its n, unlike the pronoun 'personne', which it closely resembles.

fr: Nous ne dépendons de personne pour vivre.
en: We depend on no one to live.
ipa: /nu nə de.pɑ̃.dɔ̃ də pɛʁ.sɔn puʁ vivʁ/
notes: 'personne' as object of 'de' still needs 'ne' before the verb.

fr: Il n'a aucune patience avec les enfants.
en: He has no patience with children.
ipa: /il na o.kyn pa.sjɑ̃s a.vɛk le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃/
notes: Liaison links the plural 'les' to the vowel of 'enfants'.

fr: Je ne ferai jamais confiance à cet homme.
en: I will never trust that man.
ipa: /ʒə nə fə.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s a sɛ.t‿ɔm/
notes: 'cet' is used before the vowel sound of 'homme', which has a silent h.

fr: Elle ne mange plus aucun produit laitier.
en: She no longer eats any dairy product.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃ʒ ply.z‿o.kœ̃ pʁɔ.dɥi lɛ.tje/
notes: Liaison links 'plus' and 'aucun' with a z sound before the nasal vowel.

fr: Nous n'avons entendu aucune explication claire.
en: We have not heard any clear explanation.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.tɑ̃.dy o.kyn ɛks.pli.ka.sjɔ̃ klɛʁ/
notes: 'aucune' agrees with the feminine 'explication'.

fr: Il ne se plaint jamais du travail.
en: He never complains about work.
ipa: /il nə sə plɛ̃ ʒa.mɛ dy tʁa.vaj/
notes: 'du' contracts 'de' and 'le'; it is not a separate spelling choice.

fr: Je ne connais personne d'aussi patient que lui.
en: I know no one as patient as him.
ipa: /ʒə nə kɔ.nɛ pɛʁ.sɔn do.si pa.sjɑ̃ kə lɥi/
notes: 'd'aussi' elides 'de' before the vowel-initial adverb.

fr: Elle n'a plus confiance en aucun de ses amis.
en: She no longer trusts any of her friends.
ipa: /ɛl na ply kɔ̃.fjɑ̃s ɑ̃ o.kœ̃ də se.z‿a.mi/
notes: Liaison links 'ses' and 'amis' with a z sound at the end of this long negation.

fr: Nous ne voyons aucun inconvénient à ce changement.
en: We see no problem with this change.
ipa: /nu nə vwa.jɔ̃.z‿o.kœ̃.n‿ɛ̃.kɔ̃.ve.njɑ̃ a sə ʃɑ̃ʒ.mɑ̃/
notes: Two liaisons chain here: 'voyons aucun' and 'aucun inconvénient'.

fr: Elle ne connaît que les grandes lignes de ce dossier.
en: She only knows the broad outline of this file.
ipa: /ɛl nə kɔ.nɛ kə le gʁɑ̃d liɲ də sə dɔ.sje/
notes: 'que' restricts the meaning to 'only'; don't add 'pas' alongside it.

fr: Je ne sais si cette décision était la bonne.
en: I don't know whether that decision was the right one.
ipa: /ʒə nə sɛ si sɛt de.si.zjɔ̃ e.tɛ la bɔn/
notes: This literary 'ne' can stand alone, without 'pas', after 'savoir' in careful register.

fr: Il ne cesse de se plaindre depuis son arrivée.
en: He hasn't stopped complaining since his arrival.
ipa: /il nə sɛs də sə plɛ̃dʁ də.pɥi sɔ.n‿a.ʁi.ve/
notes: Liaison links 'son' and 'arrivée' with a linking n, even in this lone-'ne' construction.

fr: Elle n'a guère apprécié la remarque de son collègue.
en: She hardly appreciated her colleague's remark.
ipa: /ɛl na gɛʁ a.pʁe.sje la ʁə.maʁk də sɔ̃ kɔ.lɛg/
notes: 'guère' means 'hardly' and replaces 'pas' in this more literary negation.

fr: Avant qu'il ne parte, nous devons régler ce détail.
en: Before he leaves, we must settle this detail.
ipa: /a.vɑ̃ kil nə paʁt nu də.vɔ̃ ʁe.gle sə de.taj/
notes: This 'ne' after 'avant que' is expletive, adding no real negation but required in formal style.

fr: Les erreurs qu'il n'a pas corrigées lui ont coûté cher.
en: The mistakes he did not correct cost him dearly.
ipa: /le.z‿e.ʁœʁ kil na pa kɔ.ʁi.ʒe lɥi ɔ̃ ku.te ʃɛʁ/
notes: The past participle 'corrigées' agrees in the feminine plural with 'erreurs', the preceding direct object.

fr: Je crains qu'elle ne se trompe de chemin.
en: I'm afraid she might take the wrong path.
ipa: /ʒə kʁɛ̃ kɛl nə sə tʁɔ̃p də ʃə.mɛ̃/
notes: After 'craindre que', this expletive 'ne' appears without expressing a true negative.

fr: Il ne nie nullement avoir commis cette erreur.
en: He does not deny at all having made that mistake.
ipa: /il nə ni nyl.mɑ̃ a.vwaʁ kɔ.mi sɛt e.ʁœʁ/
notes: 'nullement' intensifies the negation and means 'not at all', replacing 'pas'.

fr: Nous n'aurions jamais imaginé un tel résultat.
en: We would never have imagined such a result.
ipa: /nu no.ʁjɔ̃ ʒa.mɛ.z‿i.ma.ʒi.ne œ̃ tɛl ʁe.zyl.ta/
notes: Liaison links 'jamais' to 'imaginé' with a z sound in this conditional past.

fr: Elle ne saurait accepter une telle proposition.
en: She could not possibly accept such a proposal.
ipa: /ɛl nə so.ʁɛ ak.sɛp.te yn tɛl pʁɔ.po.zi.sjɔ̃/
notes: 'ne saurait' without 'pas' is a literary way to express impossibility.

fr: À moins qu'il ne pleuve, nous partirons demain.
en: Unless it rains, we'll leave tomorrow.
ipa: /a mwɛ̃ kil nə plœv nu paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ də.mɛ̃/
notes: The expletive 'ne' after 'à moins que' does not translate as a negative in English.

fr: Aucune de ces hypothèses ne semble convaincante.
en: None of these hypotheses seems convincing.
ipa: /o.kyn də se.z‿i.po.tɛz nə sɑ̃bl kɔ̃.vɛ̃.kɑ̃t/
notes: 'Aucune' as subject requires 'ne' before the verb, even at the start of the sentence.

fr: Il n'a nullement l'intention de démissionner.
en: He has no intention whatsoever of resigning.
ipa: /il na nyl.mɑ̃ lɛ̃.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃ də de.mi.sjɔ.ne/
notes: 'nullement' is spelled with a double l, unlike the related adjective 'nul'.

fr: Les documents qu'elle n'a pas signés restent en attente.
en: The documents she has not signed remain pending.
ipa: /le dɔ.ky.mɑ̃ kɛl na pa si.ɲe ʁɛst ɑ̃.n‿a.tɑ̃t/
notes: 'signés' agrees in the masculine plural with 'documents', not with the subject 'elle'.

fr: Nous avons peur qu'il ne soit trop tard pour intervenir.
en: We are afraid it may be too late to intervene.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ pœʁ kil nə swa tʁo taʁ puʁ ɛ̃.tɛʁ.və.niʁ/
notes: After 'avoir peur que', this 'ne' is expletive and does not express a real negation.

fr: Elle ne manque jamais de courage face à l'adversité.
en: She never lacks courage in the face of adversity.
ipa: /ɛl nə mɑ̃k ʒa.mɛ də ku.ʁaʒ fas a lad.vɛʁ.si.te/
notes: 'l'adversité' elides the article before the vowel-initial noun.

fr: Nous ne saurions tolérer une telle injustice.
en: We could not tolerate such an injustice.
ipa: /nu nə so.ʁjɔ̃ tɔ.le.ʁe yn tɛl ɛ̃.ʒys.tis/
notes: 'ne saurions' without 'pas' expresses a polite impossibility in formal register.

fr: Les raisons qu'il n'a jamais expliquées restent obscures.
en: The reasons he has never explained remain unclear.
ipa: /le ʁɛ.zɔ̃ kil na ʒa.mɛ.z‿ɛks.pli.ke ʁɛs.t‿ɔps.kyʁ/
notes: 'expliquées' agrees in the feminine plural with the preceding object 'raisons'.

fr: Il ne conçoit guère que l'on puisse refuser son offre.
en: He can hardly conceive that anyone would refuse his offer.
ipa: /il nə kɔ̃.swa gɛʁ kə lɔ̃ pɥis ʁə.fy.ze sɔ.n‿ɔfʁ/
notes: The nasal sound in 'conçoit' is written 'on', matching the same nasal vowel later in 'son'.

fr: Elle n'ignore pas les conséquences de son choix.
en: She is not unaware of the consequences of her choice.
ipa: /ɛl ni.ɲɔʁ pa le kɔ̃.se.kɑ̃s də sɔ̃ ʃwa/
notes: 'n'ignore pas' elides 'ne' before the vowel-initial verb, forming a litotes meaning she is well aware.

fr: Aucun argument ne l'a convaincue de changer d'avis.
en: No argument convinced her to change her mind.
ipa: /o.kœ̃.n‿aʁ.gy.mɑ̃ nə la kɔ̃.vɛ̃.ky.e də ʃɑ̃.ʒe da.vi/
notes: 'convaincue' agrees in the feminine with the preceding direct object pronoun 'l' standing for 'elle'.

fr: Je ne pense guère qu'il accepte cette offre.
en: I hardly think he'll accept this offer.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s gɛʁ kil ak.sɛpt sɛt ɔfʁ/
notes: The silent final e of the subjunctive 'accepte' must still be written after 'guère que'.

fr: Nous ne nions pas nos différends, mais nous les surmontons.
en: We do not deny our disagreements, but we overcome them.
ipa: /nu nə njɔ̃ pa no di.fe.ʁɑ̃ mɛ nu le syʁ.mɔ̃.tɔ̃/
notes: 'différends' (disagreements) is a homophone trap with 'différents' (different).

fr: Il eût fallu qu'elle ne parte pas si tôt.
en: She should not have left so early.
ipa: /il y fa.ly kɛl nə paʁt pa si to/
notes: Even in this literary construction, the full 'ne...pas' pair must be written; 'ne' alone would be incomplete here.

fr: Les objections qu'ils n'ont nullement retenues ont pourtant du poids.
en: The objections they did not consider at all still carry weight.
ipa: /le.z‿ɔb.ʒɛk.sjɔ̃ kil nɔ̃ nyl.mɑ̃ ʁə.tə.ny ɔ̃ puʁ.tɑ̃ dy pwa/
notes: 'retenues' agrees in the feminine plural with the preceding object 'objections'.

fr: Elle ne doute nullement de la loyauté de son associé.
en: She does not doubt her partner's loyalty at all.
ipa: /ɛl nə dut nyl.mɑ̃ də la lwa.jo.te də sɔ.n‿a.so.sje/
notes: Liaison links 'son' and 'associé' with a linking n.

fr: Rien ne saurait justifier un tel comportement.
en: Nothing could justify such behavior.
ipa: /ʁjɛ̃ nə so.ʁɛ ʒys.ti.fje œ̃ tɛl kɔ̃.pɔʁ.tə.mɑ̃/
notes: 'Rien' as subject still requires 'ne' before the conditional verb.

fr: Nous craignons que la situation ne s'aggrave encore.
en: We fear the situation may worsen further.
ipa: /nu kʁɛ.ɲɔ̃ kə la si.tɥa.sjɔ̃ nə sa.gʁav ɑ̃.kɔʁ/
notes: The final s of 'craignons' is silent, like all 'nous' verb endings in '-ons'.

fr: Aucune excuse n'aurait pu réparer un tel affront.
en: No excuse could have repaired such an insult.
ipa: /o.kyn ɛks.kyz no.ʁɛ py ʁe.pa.ʁe œ̃.n‿a.fʁɔ̃/
notes: Liaison links the article 'un' and 'affront' with a nasal n.
